# Web SPA (React/Vue/Angular) & SSR (Next.js/Nuxt) (`web-spa-nextjs-ssr`)

> **Group:** I. Client, Web, Mobile & Core Application Logic
> **Product Archetypes:** Web_SPA_SSR_Portal
> **Trigger Signals:** react, next, nextjs, vue, nuxt, angular, vite, webpack, dompurify, postmessage, ssr, spa

## [ BLOCK: dom-xss-and-client-sinks ]
### DOM XSS, Client-Side Routing & PostMessage Sinks
- Trace untrusted sources (`location.search`, `window.name`, `postMessage` without `event.origin` validation, API responses) into dangerous sinks (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `v-html`, `[innerHTML]`, `eval`, `document.write`, `router.push` with `javascript:` URIs).
- Check if `DOMPurify.sanitize()` is bypassed via permissive configuration (`ADD_TAGS: ['script', 'iframe']`) or mutation XSS.

## [ BLOCK: nextjs-ssr-server-actions-and-env-leak ]
### Next.js / Nuxt SSR, Server Actions, Hydration & Public Env Leakage
- Check Next.js `'use server'` actions and `getServerSideProps` / Route Handlers for missing authentication/authorization and direct internal network calls (SSRF via image optimization or server fetch).
- Inspect `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, `VITE_*`, `NUXT_PUBLIC_*`, `REACT_APP_*` environment variables and hydration payloads (`__NEXT_DATA__`) for leaked internal secrets, private API keys, or RFC1918 endpoints.

## [ BLOCK: session-storage-cors-and-csrf ]
### Token Storage (`localStorage` vs Cookies), CORS Reflection & CSRF
- Flag high-privilege JWTs/refresh tokens stored in `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` where any XSS yields full account takeover.
- Check cookie attributes (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite`) and verify whether state-changing endpoints accept cookie auth without CSRF tokens or reflect arbitrary `Origin` headers with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`.

### Standard Mappings
- ASVS-5.0-V1-Encoding-and-Sanitization, ASVS-5.0-V2-Validation-and-Business-Logic, ASVS-5.0-V7-Session-Management, ASVS-5.0-V8-Authorization, ASVS-5.0-V13-Configuration, ASVS-5.0-V14-Data-Protection, OWASP-API8:2023, CWE-79, CWE-352, CWE-918

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- Context-aware output encoding or DOMPurify.sanitize(html, { ALLOWED_TAGS: ['b', 'i', 'p', 'a'], ALLOWED_ATTR: ['href'] }) before any dangerouslySetInnerHTML / v-html / Angular DomSanitizer render
- Strict event.origin === ALLOWED_ORIGIN check and Zod/JSON schema validation on window.addEventListener('message', ...) handlers
- Next.js Server Actions ('use server') enforcing explicit session/tenant authorization guard (auth() / getServerSession) and Zod schema parsing before mutating database state
- Spring Boot @CrossOrigin(origins = {"https://portal.example.com"}, allowCredentials = "true") or NestJS app.enableCors({ origin: ['https://portal.example.com'], credentials: true }) with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax cookies
- Next.js next.config.js images.remotePatterns restricted to pinned CDN hostnames and server-only secrets imported via 'server-only' package without NEXT_PUBLIC_ / VITE_ / NUXT_PUBLIC_ prefixes
- URL navigation helpers validating protocol allowlist (new URL(target).protocol === 'https:') before passing user-controlled links to router.push(), window.location.assign(), or <a href>

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Unfiltered dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: userContent }}, Vue v-html="rawHtml", or Angular bypassSecurityTrustHtml() bound to API/URL parameters without DOMPurify sanitization
- window.addEventListener('message', (e) => { eval(e.data); router.push(e.data.redirectUrl); }) without validating e.origin against an explicit allowlist
- Secrets or internal service tokens prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_ / VITE_ / REACT_APP_ / NUXT_PUBLIC_ bundled into client JS or serialized into __NEXT_DATA__ hydration state
- Next.js Server Actions ('use server') or Nuxt server/api/* routes mutating database records by ID without verifying getServerSession() / caller tenant ownership inside the action body
- NestJS app.enableCors({ origin: true, credentials: true }) or Spring Boot @CrossOrigin(origins = "*", allowCredentials = "true") combined with localStorage.setItem('access_token', jwt)
- Next.js SSR getServerSideProps / Route Handlers fetching user-supplied URLs or Host/X-Forwarded-Host headers directly, enabling SSRF to 169.254.169.254 or internal 10.x services

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt showing exact source-to-sink dataflow in React/Vue/Angular component, template, or postMessage listener
- ev_... excerpt of Next.js Server Action ('use server') or SSR loader showing authentication/authorization checks and input validation
- ev_... excerpt of next.config.js / vite.config.ts / nuxt.config.ts showing public environment variables and image/proxy domains
- ev_... excerpt of CORS middleware, CSRF token verification, and cookie/localStorage token storage implementation

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Is a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) with nonce/hash enforcement and without unsafe-inline / unsafe-eval injected at the CDN or reverse proxy?
- Are Next.js Server Actions and /_next/data routes protected by a global middleware.ts matcher that fails closed on unauthenticated requests?
- Are cookie-authenticated state-changing endpoints protected by SameSite=Strict/Lax plus an anti-CSRF synchronizer token or custom header check?
- Does the build pipeline strip or reject server-side secrets if accidentally referenced in client-side bundles?
